body: Thursday, February 19 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Activity is firm enough to keep the Fed patient: January payrolls rose by 130,000 and unemployment fell to 4.3%, January CPI rose 2.4%, less than expected, and the AI boom is underpinning business spending on equipment while housing stays weak. The Fed's own tone is the news: the January minutes show no rush to restart cuts and even a possibility of hikes, with officials split on the path.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.47% and the 10Y at 4.09%, a +62 bps spread; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 13 bps and the 10Y 21 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) that leaves the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, though the 2Y rose 2 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18). Yields rose as the minutes showed disagreement on the next cut. The S&P 500 closed at 6,881.31, up 0.56%, and the VIX at 19.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

New / Most Important: Equities shrugged off the hawkish tilt: Wall Street ended higher, lifted by Nvidia and other AI stocks. A Fed debating hikes makes the front end, not the long end, the vulnerable part of the curve.

Playbook ✓: Trim 2Y exposure but keep core IEF while the 20-observation move is still a bull flattening; in equities, favour AI suppliers and industrials over rate-sensitive small caps. Change the call if core services inflation cools, or if the 2Y breaks above its 20-observation-ago 3.60% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).

Macro Stance: Europe remains the rotation winner: the STOXX 600 closed at a record 628.69, up 4.32% over 20 sessions, and the FTSE 100 at 10,686.20, up 5.41% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Reuters credits an earnings boost, while US stocks are off to their worst start versus the global market since 1995.

Activity & Inflation: UK inflation fell to 3.0%, its lowest in nearly a year, strengthening bets on a Bank of England cut; GBP/USD slipped 0.46% to 1.3564 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The DAX rose 1.12% to 25,278.21 as German exporters joined the rally (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

New / Most Important: The ECB says no decision has been made on Lagarde's potential early exit, but succession talk already puts Knot and De Cos in the frame. A hawkish successor would firm the euro, which closed at 1.1852 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight European equities versus the US, add UK domestics and gilts on the inflation drop, and keep a partial EUR hedge until the succession is settled. Downgrade if the STOXX 600 falls back below its five-session-ago level, which would mark the record as a squeeze rather than a trend.

Macro Stance: Mainland markets are shut for the Lunar New Year, so the read rests on January data and holiday spending. Xi prioritised 'AI-plus' and consumer spending to counter economic risks, but the data still show weak credit demand and falling home prices. The macro stance stays bearish; the holiday is the near-term test.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official read is the January manufacturing PMI, which dropped to 49.3, back in contraction. The feed carries no fresh activity print during the holiday, so the services tilt is unproven; a February PMI back above 50 would be the first confirmation, and a second sub-50 reading would push Beijing toward broader stimulus.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists, so the seasonal credit surge was smaller than hoped. With household borrowing soft, the credit impulse is being carried by policy lending rather than private demand; a beat in household loans would change the view.

Property: Housing still has no floor: SCMP reports home prices keep falling despite policy support. Falling prices keep households paying down mortgages instead of borrowing, which is consistent with the weak January loan data. Two consecutive months of stable new-home prices in the largest cities would be needed to call a bottom.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The IMF warned that China's economic policies are causing damage to others, a reminder that export-led growth invites trade pushback from partners. Policy support is being steered toward services and technology rather than a broad infrastructure push, which spreads the impulse thinly and keeps the near-term growth lift modest.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng's last pre-holiday close was 26,705.94, up 0.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16), capping what SCMP called the best lunar-year performance in eight years. The Shanghai Composite last closed at 4,082.07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). US-listed proxies rose in the prior session: ASHR closed at 34.01 (+1.58% over 20 sessions), FXI at 38.72 and KWEB at 32.89, still down 5.95% over 20 sessions, while USD/CNY held at 6.9080, down 0.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

New / Most Important: Holiday demand is the bright spot: China's Spring Festival box office exceeded 2 bln yuan. Strong services spending fits Beijing's consumption pivot, but it has not yet shown up in credit or goods prices. Watch the onshore reopening: a strong start for consumer and travel names would support the services story, a fade would confirm the bearish macro read.

Playbook ✓: Underweight broad China beta (FXI, KWEB) until the official PMI regains 50; own consumption and AI-plus leaders in Hong Kong only on pullbacks, and avoid developers while prices keep falling. ⚠ Divergence: Hong Kong's best lunar-year run in eight years and record holiday box office contradict the weak credit and PMI data — sentiment is running ahead of the numbers.

Macro Stance: Takaichi was formally elected prime minister and is eyeing expedited budget deliberation, while exports rose the most in three years as AI demand underpins chips. The risk is fiscal: two-thirds of Japanese firms are concerned about the prime minister's fiscal discipline, so the reflation trade now depends on how the budget is funded.

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 57,143.84, up 1.02% and 7.84% over 20 sessions, while USD/JPY closed at 153.149, down 3.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The Fed said last month's 'rate checks' were made at the Treasury's request, which confirms Washington's sensitivity to yen weakness and caps USD/JPY upside.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities with a tilt to exporters exposed to AI chips and to banks, and keep fading USD/JPY rallies toward its 20-session-ago 158.162 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Turn neutral if the budget leans on deficit-funded tax cuts that push long JGB yields sharply higher.

Macro Stance: The unemployment rate held at 4.1%, prompting talk of another RBA rate rise. At the same time economic confidence hit a 13-year low as immigration concerns escalated, so the RBA faces a tight labour market alongside a fragile mood.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7083, up 5.22% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 9,007.00, up 2.17% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Consumer-facing earnings are softening: Wesfarmers shares dropped on a retail miss, a sign that higher rates are reaching household spending.

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD against USD on the hike risk, but underweight consumer discretionary names on the ASX and prefer miners and banks with pricing power. Turn bearish on the AUD if unemployment rises from 4.1% in the next print, which would take another hike off the table.

Monetary & Activity: Growth accelerated into year-end (Rzeczpospolita: 'Gospodarka Polski przyspieszyła w IV kwartale' — the economy sped up in Q4), and January CPI came in at 2.2% y/y. The print was above forecasts, but the MPC is seen closer to a March cut (300Gospodarka: 'RPP bliżej marcowej obniżki stóp').

FX & Markets: Bankier describes a 'fiesta' in Polish debt and asks whether to join the bond rally ('Trwa fiesta na rynku polskiego długu'). EUR/PLN closed at 4.2167 and USD/PLN at 3.5559, down 1.25% over 20 sessions; EPOL rose 0.61% to 37.73 and the WIG20TR ETF 1.73% to 67.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). KGHM rebounded 5.92% to 302.20 and PGE is up 16.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Companies: Orlen reported a large rise in annual net profit (Interia: 'Duży wzrost rocznego zysku netto'), and Orlen shares (PKN) are up 9.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). KGHM's EUR 6 billion copper agreement with NKT adds multi-year volume visibility, and Pekao is up 10.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Security & New Development: The EU approved €44 billion in SAFE defence loans for Poland, financing a procurement wave that favours local production. The cost is a wider deficit, so the bond rally depends on inflation staying near target.

Playbook ✓: Own Polish banks (Pekao, PKO) and PGE for the March-cut and growth trade, and add Orlen on earnings momentum; hold zloty exposure unhedged. ⚠ Divergence: January inflation came in above forecasts while the bond market celebrates — a second upside surprise would hit the front end first.

Narrative: The software sell-off is turning into dispersion: XLK closed at 140.91, up 1.03% in the prior session and down only 0.66% over 20, while Oracle is still down 13.2% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Adobe has dropped 26% as Wall Street questions its defence against AI competition.

Reported: Figma's stock jumped 15% as the company sees AI monetisation accelerating growth — the first clear case of a software name beating and rallying on AI. Apple closed at 264.35, up 7.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Morgan Stanley calls Microsoft the most under-owned stock; at 399.60 and down 12.08% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), it has the most room for a positive surprise among the mega caps if cloud demand holds.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Figma's rally shows the market will pay for software that monetises AI rather than being replaced by it. Own AI-monetising platforms and under-owned mega caps, and avoid seat-based incumbents until their guidance proves the moat.

Narrative: Communication services split between AI spenders and pressured media names: XLC closed at 114.59, up 0.99% over 20 sessions, with Meta up 6.47% but Alphabet down 5.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Meta's multiyear deal for millions of Nvidia chips keeps its spend escalating.

Reported: Disney issued $4 billion in corporate bonds for the first time since 2020, and the stock rose 1.57% to 107.10 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Credit markets remain open to cash-generative media names.

EPS Upside Watch: Netflix, at 77.99 and down 10.62% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), is the de-rated candidate for a positive surprise, with subscription revenue that AI tools do not obviously threaten.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Media and tech are re-levering at once: Disney's bond deal and hyperscaler chip commitments add supply to a credit market already wary of AI capex. If spreads widen, cash-rich names re-rate relative to borrowers.

Narrative: Banks are fine; private credit is not. XLF closed at 52.59, up 0.75% in the prior session, and Goldman Sachs rose 1.93% to 933.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The +62 bps curve still supports lending margins (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).

Reported: The FT reports Blue Owl permanently halted redemptions at a private credit fund aimed at retail investors, the most concrete sign yet of liquidity stress in the asset class. Bank of America rose 1.18% to 53.36 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Money-centre banks with trading desks gain from volatility and heavy issuance; JPMorgan closed at 308.78, up 2.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). They are also the natural buyers of assets that private funds need to sell.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consensus treats private credit as a structural share-taker from banks; a gated retail fund turns that around. Deposit-funded balance sheets now look like the safer way to own credit growth, so prefer banks over alternative managers and BDCs.

Narrative: The geopolitical premium is back: oil jumped 4% after Vance said Iran ignored key US demands and military strikes are on the table. Brent closed at $70.35, up 4.35%, and XLE at 54.78, up 15.08% over 20 sessions, with Exxon up 15.5% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Reported: Occidental Petroleum topped quarterly profit estimates on midstream support, showing integrated cash flows can beat even at modest crude prices. Exxon rose 3.07% to 150.68 and Chevron 1.84% to 183.87 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).
EPS Upside Watch: If Brent holds near $70.35, Q1 producer estimates have upside (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Midstream-heavy names carry the least commodity risk into any reversal.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Business Insider notes oil jumped on geopolitical fear while a massive glut sits at sea. Without an actual supply disruption, the physical surplus pulls crude back, so energy equities that have already run 15.08% in 20 sessions are a hedge, not a core overweight (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Narrative: Industrials have earnings support from AI-linked capex: XLI closed at 175.04, up 7.04% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar at 751.97, up 19.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Reuters reports the AI boom is underpinning business spending on equipment.

Reported: BAE Systems forecast years of growth in a 'new era' of defence spending as its backlog hit a record. GE closed at 329.58, up 5.52% over 20 sessions, while Boeing fell 2.09% to 238.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Defence primes with record backlogs and equipment makers tied to data-centre power have the clearest estimate upside; BAE's backlog gives multi-year revenue visibility. Caterpillar's 19.55% 20-session gain shows the market already rewards power-generation exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Caterpillar fell 1.67% in the prior session while the S&P 500 rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18): the crowded machinery trade is starting to churn. Rotate within the sector toward defence and electrical equipment rather than adding to the most extended names.

Narrative: Discretionary is still the laggard: XLY closed at 117.02, down 1.76% over 20 sessions, with Amazon down 11.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Barron's notes Amazon just snapped its worst losing streak since 2006, but that is a capex-fear relief, not a consumer upgrade.

Reported: DoorDash stock climbed 14%, reversing a plunge after an earnings and revenue miss, a sign the market is now buying beaten-down platform names. Home Depot closed at 383.52 and Tesla at 411.32 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Housing-linked names could surprise if starts keep rising: US housing starts rose to a five-month high in a broad increase. Home Depot is up 2.24% over 20 sessions and Nike 3.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), the two most leveraged to a rate-relief consumer.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Higher housing starts cut against the consumer gloom, but a Fed debating hikes caps the mortgage relief housing needs. Until the path clears, the Amazon and DoorDash rebounds are positioning trades, not a fundamental turn.

Narrative: Staples have rallied as bond proxies: XLP closed at 88.04, up 6.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Walmart reports Q4 earnings on Thursday, the sector's biggest test.

Reported: Kenvue surged on an earnings beat as its Kimberly-Clark merger gains steam, showing deal-driven staples still get paid. Walmart fell 1.73% to 126.62 and Costco 1.58% to 996.08 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart's scale and higher-income customer gains make it the most likely upside print; a five-session change of -0.06% shows the stock has already given back its recent gains into the report (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples rose with falling yields, but the Fed minutes have pushed yields up; the 10Y at 4.09% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18) is the real risk to the group, more than any single earnings print.

Narrative: Healthcare is range-bound: XLV closed at 157.67, up 1.46% over 20 sessions, with Eli Lilly down 1.5% to 1,020.56 and UnitedHealth down 14.84% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Axios reports Trump officials are trying to make peace with pharma.

Reported: Pharma signals it is done negotiating as Trump's drug-pricing effort marches on, which keeps policy risk alive even as the tone softens. UnitedHealth is up 5.48% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), a rebound in managed care.

EPS Upside Watch: Managed care is the rebound candidate if medical-cost trends stabilise; UnitedHealth at 288.20 remains far below its 20-session-ago 338.43 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Large-cap pharma with obesity exposure keeps the steadiest estimate path.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A pricing truce would remove the main overhang on large-cap pharma just as investors rotate into defensives. If the truce holds, Lilly and the managed-care names are cheaper ways to own defence than staples priced as bond proxies.

Narrative: Materials lead the market: XLB closed at 53.02, up 10.02% over 20 sessions, as copper rose 2.85% to $5.79/lb and gold 2.11% to $5,009.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Reuters says copper climbed on dip-buying and a recovery in tech shares, tying the metal to AI and grid capex.

Reported: Glencore will return $2 billion to shareholders despite an earnings dip, and the miners' copper exposure is offsetting coal and iron ore weakness. Freeport rose 2.39% to 62.55 and Newmont 1.95% to 124.69 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners have the most operating leverage with gold at $5,009.50, up 5.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18); Q1 realised prices point to estimate upgrades for low-cost producers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver rebounded 5.53% in the prior session but is still down 17.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18): the speculative metal is lagging the industrial and monetary ones. Own copper and gold producers, not silver.

Narrative: Real estate lost its tailwind for a day: XLRE fell 1.34% to 43.35 but is still up 4.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), as Treasury yields rose on the Fed minutes.
Reported: CareTrust REIT launched a $1.0 billion at-the-market equity programme with forward sales, using the rally to raise capital — a sign landlords see the equity window as open.

EPS Upside Watch: Healthcare and senior-housing REITs that can raise equity at a premium, as CareTrust is doing, have the clearest external-growth path. The 30Y at 4.71% is the funding benchmark (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Equity issuance into a rally often marks a near-term top for the group, and a Fed that discusses hikes removes the rate-cut leg of the REIT thesis. Prefer issuers with external growth over plain rate-sensitive office and retail landlords.

Narrative: Utilities paused after a strong run: XLU fell 1.66% to 45.61 but is up 6.17% over 20 sessions, while Constellation fell 2.96% in the prior session and is still up 8.45% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Data-centre load growth remains the driver.

Reported: The US grid reliability watchdog will recommend rules for data centres, which formalises how large loads connect and should make contracted-load utilities more investable. Vistra closed at 170.57, up 8.77% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).
EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with contracted large loads have the most visible rate-base growth; NextEra closed at 91.22, up 9.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Grid rules could also force data centres to bring their own power or pay more for connection, shifting returns from utilities to on-site generation. Prefer regulated wires-and-pipes names over merchant generators priced for unlimited AI demand.

Narrative: European autos are grinding higher on restructuring hopes: the STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts tracker closed at 46.55, up 3.64% over 20 sessions, with BMW up 5.83% and Volkswagen preference shares up 5.3% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Cost cuts, not demand, are what the market is buying.

Reported: Bloomberg reports Jeep's owner Stellantis has a $17 billion reliability problem, a fresh overhang ahead of its results. Renault rose 1.75% to 33.19 and is up 5.37% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Premium OEMs with pricing power look best placed: Mercedes-Benz closed at 59.40 and BMW at 91.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Stellantis announces full-year 2025 results on February 26, the next test for the sector.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stellantis is up 4.81% over five sessions but down 16.24% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18) despite a $17 billion reliability issue — relief rallies in damaged names suggest short-covering rather than a demand recovery.

Narrative: Semis lead on scarcity: SOXX closed at 357.92, up 6.1% over 20 sessions, with Micron up 5.3% in the prior session and 15.33% over 20, and ASML up 10.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Meta's multiyear deal for millions of Nvidia chips underwrites accelerator demand.

Reported: Analog Devices sees a strong second quarter as the AI boom fuels chip sales, extending the AI trade into analog and industrial chips. TSMC ADRs closed at 362.26, up 10.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

EPS Upside Watch: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25; the stock closed at 187.98, up 1.63% and 5.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Memory makers have the cleanest revision path while the shortage persists.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AMD closed at 200.12, down 13.71% over 20 sessions while Micron rose 15.33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18): within semis the market pays for scarce memory, equipment and analog rather than accelerator challengers.

Rewarded: Companies that showed AI monetisation or returned capital were rewarded: Figma jumped 15% on accelerating AI monetisation, Analog Devices rose on a strong AI-driven outlook, and Glencore will return $2 billion despite an earnings dip. Kenvue surged on a beat and merger progress, and DoorDash reversed its post-earnings plunge with a 14% gain.

Punished: Wesfarmers dropped on a retail miss, a warning on household spending. Adobe is down 26% on doubts about its defence against AI, the clearest case of a franchise priced for disruption regardless of near-term numbers. Caterpillar slipped 1.67% even as the S&P 500 rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), a sign that crowded winners are being trimmed.

Pattern: The 'beat and fall' regime of early February is easing: the market now rewards companies that show AI revenue or hand back cash, and it buys beaten-down platforms once the selling exhausts. It still punishes consumer misses and incumbents whose moat AI could erode.

Attention into EPS: Walmart's Q4 print lands Thursday, and Nvidia reports on Feb. 25: the two results test the consumer and the AI-capex trade. In Europe, Stellantis's full-year results on February 26 test the autos rally.

Playbook: Buy AI monetisers and capital returners on post-print weakness, and keep avoiding consumer names that miss. Into Walmart and Nvidia, express views with defined-risk options rather than outright stock. Revisit if Nvidia's guide disappoints, which would reverse the semis leadership that is carrying the AI trade.

Attention Gap: Morgan Stanley calls Microsoft the most under-owned stock, after a 12.08% 20-session decline that left it at 399.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Figma's 15% jump on AI monetisation shows the market will re-rate software that proves AI adds revenue rather than replacing seats.

Exposure & Risk: Own MSFT and a small basket of AI-monetising application vendors against a short in seat-based incumbents. Risk: another frontier-model release that triggers a fresh sector-wide sell-off before earnings can prove the case.

Attention Gap: BAE Systems' record backlog and forecast of years of growth and the EU's €44 billion of SAFE loans for Poland show a funded European procurement cycle. Attention still sits on US primes rather than European producers and suppliers.

Exposure & Risk: Express through European aerospace-and-defence names with munitions and air-defence content. Risk: a Russia–Ukraine settlement would hit sentiment before it hits backlogs, but the latest Geneva talks ended without a breakthrough, which keeps that risk distant.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was $66,425.32, down 1.58% on the day, 3.53% over five sessions and 21.45% over 20; ether closed at $1,953.97 (-30.67% over 20 sessions) and solana at $81.57, down 4.26% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). IBIT closed at 37.54, down 2.21%, Coinbase at 164.05 and Strategy at 125.20, down 2.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

New / Most Important: CoinDesk says losing $70,000 is a warning sign for further downside. Institutions are split: Abu Dhabi funds added to bitcoin bets despite the rout, while Brevan Howard cut its bitcoin ETF holding and expanded its options position — hedged exposure rather than outright conviction.

Playbook: Stay underweight until bitcoin reclaims $70,000; prefer IBIT to MSTR or COIN, and express any upside view with options, as Brevan Howard is doing. The geopolitical risk-off that lifted gold did not lift bitcoin, so it is not acting as a hedge.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 97.70, up 0.56% and 0.93% over five sessions, while TLT fell 0.38% to 89.53 and IEF 0.21% to 97.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Yields rose as the minutes showed disagreement on the next cut, and the 2Y is up 2 bps over five observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).

Credit Check: HYG closed at 80.91, up 0.04% over 20 sessions, and LQD at 111.59, up 1.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), so public credit is calm. Under the surface, Seeking Alpha flags a surge in short bets on LQD and HYG on AI-capex fears, and Blue Owl's gated retail fund shows liquidity stress in private credit.

Portfolio Implication: Hold investment grade over high yield and avoid semi-liquid private-credit vehicles. Keep the dollar underweight small while the Fed debates hikes. Add duration only if the 10Y returns toward its 20-observation-ago 4.30% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).

What Is Priced: Oil settled up 4% on Iran-US tensions as Russia-Ukraine talks ended without a breakthrough, and the NYT reports the US military is moving into place for possible strikes. Brent closed at $70.35 and gold at $5,009.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).

Conditional Expression: If strikes happen, crude and gold gap higher: own short-dated USO calls and gold miners, and underweight airlines. If diplomacy resumes, the 4.35% Brent jump reverses quickly (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), so fade XLE strength rather than chase it.
Risk: A massive oil glut at sea means any premium fades fast without a real supply loss, so the long-oil leg must be optionality, not outright futures.

What Is Priced: Markets were waiting on US GDP alongside the Fed minutes, and the minutes showed no rush to restart cuts and even a possibility of hikes. The 2Y at 3.47% still sits below the 3M bill at 3.70% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18).
